design.title: Design system
design.lead: One vocabulary, held to a number rather than to taste. Every value on this page is read out of the application's own tokens.
design.coloursBody: Named for their role, never their appearance. A theme is one assignment because each name is a reference into the palette in force.
design.rampBody: Not themeable. These eight are document data, written into every project file, so repainting them would make a saved project disagree with the swatch it was chosen from.
design.liftBody: How much lighter a surface gets when touched. A large surface needs a subtler lift than a small one — that distinction is real, and the other values that had grown beside it were not.
design.galleryCaption: The whole design system on one page, rendered by dew_shot gallery.

home.intro: A channel rack with a step grid, a piano roll, a playlist of clips and a mixer, driven by a three-oscillator synth per channel — or by a recording, or by a song written as text and compiled to notes.
home.tabsBody: The same notes, seen four ways, and a fifth tab that writes them for you.

mcp.title: Control dew from an agent
mcp.lead: dew runs a Model Context Protocol server inside the application, so a coding agent can read and change the project you have open - instruments, effects, the mixer, the notes and the arrangement.
mcp.howBody: Turn it on under Audio > MCP. dew listens on the loopback interface only, and nothing off your machine can reach it. The first time a client connects, dew names it and asks whether to allow it - and whether it may only read, or change things too. Every change it makes is one step of your undo history.
mcp.connectBody: The MCP settings panel shows the address and the exact command. The port is not fixed: dew takes the next free one when its own is busy, so copy the command rather than typing it.
mcp.surfaceBody: One address space covers every value in the document. A target, an id, a group and a slot name any parameter of any oscillator, envelope, sample, soundfont, effect, mixer insert or the master - and the same four fields say what a curve can be pointed at.
mcp.scoreBody: For anything longer than a few bars, an agent writes dew’s arrangement language and compiles it. The language says what the music is - a key, a progression, rhythms, voicings, a counterpoint - and the compiler works out the notes.

mcpReference.title: MCP reference
mcpReference.lead: Generated from the same table the server dispatches on and the permission check reads, so a tool cannot exist without being documented and cannot be documented differently from how it behaves.
mcpReference.guideLead: dew serves these as MCP resources. A client should read the first before its first call.
mcpReference.undoNote: Every call that changes the project is exactly one undo step, however many entries its batch carried.

score.title: The score language
score.lead: A song written as text and compiled to real patterns, notes and clips. Seven block keywords, and the set is closed.
score.exampleCaption: examples/amber.score — the one CI compiles and renders.
score.noExpressions: There is no expression language — no arithmetic, no variables, no conditionals. That single restriction is what makes completion a table lookup rather than type inference, and what lets the grid be computed statically before anything is generated.

setup.title: Setup
setup.lead: dew builds from source on macOS in three commands. There is no release to download: it is a working prototype, and the thing you would be downloading is a build of this repository.
setup.requirementsBody: macOS, and nothing that is not already on a machine somebody writes software on. brew bundle installs the rest from the Brewfile in the repository root.
setup.buildBody: The first configure fetches JUCE and Catch2 from source — a few seconds, shallow, cached per machine under ~/.cache/CPM — so one build is slow and the rest are not.
setup.presetsBody: Presets rather than raw flags, so the flags a build was made with are in the repository rather than in somebody's shell history.
setup.runBody: Then Demos → Getting Started in the menu bar. There are eight, and each one is the demo for a different part of the app rather than eight versions of the same song.
setup.checkBody: One command, running everything CI runs, in the order that fails cheapest first: the dependency pins and the formatting need no build, so a bad pin or an unformatted file is reported in seconds rather than after a compile.
setup.platformNote: macOS only. Nothing here has been built or run on another platform, and the parts that could be — the score language compiles under gcc and libstdc++ in CI — are the parts that link nothing.
